title: Fix _cf_helpers.mjs's numeric child_profile_id fixture so listTutorGrants' outgoing-mode test can assert real behavior

evidence.quote:
// A length assertion would be fragile due to type coercion in Firestore.
    assert.ok(res.grants !== undefined);

why: res.grants is always an array (never undefined) per listTutorGrants' own return contract, so `assert.ok(res.grants !== undefined)` cannot fail regardless of whether the outgoing-mode query is correct -- the test labeled 'outgoing mode happy path' gives zero regression protection for that query path. The comment is honest about why (seedActiveGrant stores child_profile_id as a JS number, while inviteTutor -- every real production writer -- requires and stores it as a string, so the '==' query never matches the fixture), but the fix belongs in the shared fixture, not in weakening the assertion, and the weakening carries no `// weaken-ok:` tag per the standard.
recommendation: Change seedActiveGrant to store child_profile_id: String(PROFILE), matching every production writer, then strengthen the assertion to check res.grants.length === 1 and the returned grant's fields.
acceptance_criteria: The 'outgoing mode happy path' test asserts res.grants.length === 1 and fails if the outgoing query breaks.

corrections: Minor rule mislabel: git log -p shows this assertion was authored weak in its original commit (b93e1d2c), never a prior stronger assertion that got weakened. TQ-7 ('never weaken a test') is a slight misfit; TQ-8 ('tautological tests... assertions weaker than what the source can do wrong') matches the actual defect more precisely. Does not change the verdict.
